transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because my eating has gotten out of hand. After everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers, but then I’ll end up eating a really large amount—like half a tray of catered pasta, dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks are in the pantry, all in one sitting.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food in one sitting happen?
For the last three months, it’s been happening at least one night almost every week. Usually it’s after an argument or when I get home late from a work event. Some weeks it happens twice.
How do you feel after one of these episodes of eating a large amount of food in one sitting?

Afterward I feel really embarrassed and kind of disgusted with myself. I’ll sit there thinking I’ve ruined this disciplined version of myself I try so hard to keep up, and that I should’ve gone for a run or done yoga instead of doing that.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yes. Once I start, especially after a tense night with my husband, it feels like I can’t really make myself stop. I’ll be thinking, “Patricia, stop, that’s enough,” but I just keep reaching for more anyway.
Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating by doing things like vomiting, using laxatives, or fasting?
I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t think I’ve really done things like that, at least not in any planned way. I mostly just feel awful afterward and try to move on.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past three months?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been tracking it closely, and I don’t think I’ve noticed a big change, but I can’t say for certain.
Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating by exercising excessively?
I don’t think so. I’m not really someone who goes and works out hard to make up for it. I might tell myself I should be better or move more, but I don’t do excessive exercise after.
Do you often feel guilty after these episodes of eating a large amount of food?

Yes. I usually feel really guilty afterward. Mostly embarrassed and kind of disgusted with myself, like I’ve ruined this disciplined person I’m trying to be. I’ll sit there thinking I should’ve gone for a run or done yoga instead.
Have you ever engaged in any behaviors to try to counteract the calories you consumed during these episodes?

I’m not sure exactly what counts. I don’t make myself throw up or take anything, if that’s what you mean. I might think about trying to be more controlled afterward, but I don’t really do something specific to cancel it out.
Do you ever restrict your food intake on the days following one of these episodes?
I’m not really sure. I might tell myself I should eat “better” the next day, but I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where I deliberately restrict or skip meals after.
Do you worry about gaining weight as a result of these episodes of eating a large amount of food in one sitting?

I’m not totally sure. I don’t usually think of it in a specific way like, “I’m going to gain weight from this,” but I do feel bad about what I ate and worry a bit about what it means. It’s more just a general uncomfortable feeling afterward.
Do you ever use diuretics to try to counteract the calories you consumed during these episodes?
No, I don’t use diuretics. I don’t really do anything like that after those episodes.
Do you worry about how your body looks after one of these eating episodes?

I’m not sure I focus on my body looks specifically right after. I mostly just feel uncomfortable and kind of upset with myself, but I haven’t really noticed myself checking my body or worrying about my appearance in a clear way.
Do you fear gaining weight as a result of these episodes of eating?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’m clearly afraid of gaining weight after it, at least not in a way I can point to. I just feel uneasy and regretful afterward, but it’s not always specifically about weight.
Do you think your eating episodes are related to concerns about your weight or how your body looks?

I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed a clear link to my weight or how my body looks. It feels more like I get into the episode and then feel bad afterward, but I can’t say it’s because of body image concerns.
Do you think the feeling of being disgusted with yourself after these episodes is related to a fear of gaining weight?

Maybe partly, but it feels more like I’m disgusted with myself for losing control. I feel embarrassed, like I’ve blown this image of being disciplined. I’ll sit there thinking I should’ve gone for a run or done yoga instead of eating like that.
Do you feel like you have no control over your eating during these episodes?

Yes. Once I start, especially after a tense night with my husband, it feels like the decision-making part of me just shuts off. I keep reaching for more food even while I’m thinking, “Patricia, stop, this is enough.”
Have you experienced any noticeable weight fluctuations over the past three months?
I’m not really sure. I don’t weigh myself regularly, so I haven’t noticed any clear changes over the last three months.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these episodes of eating?
I’m not really sure how to answer that right now. I don’t have anything clear to add about that.
Do you ever use fasting as a way to make up for eating a large amount of food during one of these episodes?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it that way, so I don’t have a clear answer.
